rules.text: If each category's adjacent printed percentage is the dashboard's current labeled rating-share value, and the public follow-up rule requires selecting the category with the highest such labeled value, then the eligible form option corresponding to the uniquely largest printed percentage is the required category selection.
rules.component: chart label/category binding and task-to-action relation
rules.conditions: The printed percentages are authoritative labeled rating-share values, each is attached to the category beneath its mark, and the task's specified decision rule governs this form.

rules.text: If the vertical positions of the plotted dots on the axis labeled "Value" encode the same decision metric that the task calls current labeled rating share, then the highest-positioned dot supplies a competing ranking; a disagreement between that ranking and the adjacent printed percentages leaves the proposed selection dependent on resolving which encoding is authoritative.
rules.conditions: This conditional reading applies only if the y-axis geometry, rather than the printed percentage labels, is intended to encode the task's decision metric.

observations.content: The dot above "Quality" has the printed inscription "24%", and the dot above "Price" has the printed inscription "10%."

task_evidence.content: Select the category with the highest current labeled rating share

chains.claim: Conditionally, the printed 52% attached to Design is larger than every other displayed category percentage, so the stated highest-current-labeled-rating-share rule supports Select Design.

observations.content: The chart title is inscribed "Product Rating Share by Category", and the vertical axis is inscribed "Value" with ticks from 0 through 65.
The dot above "Quality" is visibly higher on the page, near the 60 tick, than the dot above "Design", which is near the 42 level.

observations.location: labels adjacent to Quality and Design dots
observations.content: The Quality dot has the printed inscription "24%" and the Design dot has the printed inscription "52%."

task_evidence.content: Use the dashboard labeled rating-share values as the evidence source; the follow-up queue is reserved for the category with the strongest current customer feedback signal.

chains.claim: The dots' vertical positions visibly rank Quality above Design while their adjacent printed percentages rank Design above Quality. Because the task specifically names labeled rating-share values, this does not establish a different selection, but it leaves the proposal conditional on treating the printed labels rather than the y-axis geometry as the authoritative decision-metric encoding.

refinements.condition_note: If the Design selection supported by this chain is used to complete the form, the three required companion fields must also be set to Open product feedback follow-up, Prioritize highest current rating share, and Product operations feedback follow-up queue.
refinements.reason: This adds the public workflow-completion requirements that follow the category decision and are not represented in the original category-selection chain.

question_responses.reason: The refinement extends the existing conditional support for Select Design with the three required companion-field selections needed for form completion; it does not alter the chart-based category conclusion.
